title: Android Malware ML Classifier
description: Automated pipeline for gathering Android malware samples, training machine learning models on extracted feature vectors, and plotting classification accuracy. Supports multiple feature extraction strategies — XML-based permissions, system call traces, disassembled API calls, and ssdeep fuzzy hashes — with TensorFlow neural networks and scikit-learn SVM/decision tree alternatives.

title: theZoo — Live Malware Repository
description: Open malware database designed to make malware analysis accessible to security researchers. Provides a CLI-driven interface to browse, search, and retrieve live malware samples and source code in an organized, encrypted format for safe educational research and threat intelligence work.

title: GoART — Atomic Red Team Executor
description: Standalone Go application that packages MITRE ATT&CK atomic test definitions directly into the binary for execution in air-gapped or internet-restricted environments. Executes atomic tests across Windows, macOS, and Linux, enabling adversary simulation without external dependencies. Supports local test development by loading custom atomics from a local directory.

title: Invoke-AtomicRedTeam
description: PowerShell module for executing MITRE ATT&CK atomic tests across Windows, macOS, and Linux environments. Enables security teams to run controlled adversary simulations against their own infrastructure to validate detection, alerting, and incident response capabilities.

title: Malware Analysis Sandbox
description: Python-based automated sandbox for analyzing malware behavior in a secure, isolated environment. Tracks file system changes, registry modifications, and network activity during controlled execution. Integrates with Cuckoo Sandbox and VirtualBox/VMware to automate sample submission, monitoring, and comprehensive behavioral report generation.

title: Google Cybersecurity Certificate Labs
description: Hands-on labs and projects from the Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate covering security audits, network defense, incident response, and SIEM operations. Includes practical work with Wireshark, tcpdump, Suricata IDS, Splunk, and Chronicle SIEM for threat detection and packet analysis.

title: Linux Kernel Exploit Research (FUZE)
description: Research into Linux kernel Use-After-Free vulnerabilities using the FUZE framework — a tool combining critical information extraction, context-aware kernel fuzzing, and partial symbolic execution to facilitate kernel exploit generation. Dependencies include angr, pwntools, ROPGadget, and KASAN for dynamic analysis.

title: Black Hat India 2026 — Advanced Malware Traffic Analysis
description: Intensive hands-on training at Black Hat India 2026 covering end-to-end malware traffic analysis. Worked through 8 modules spanning networking fundamentals, traffic methodology using Wireshark/tcpdump/tshark/Zeek, threat intelligence with OSINT, ransomware detection, live exploit traffic analysis (CVE-2021-41773 Apache RCE), NetFlow/SIEM hunting in Splunk, and ML-based anomaly detection using Slips and Zeek Anomaly Detector.

title: Red vs Blue Team Assessment
description: Full-cycle security engagement combining offensive and defensive operations. Red Team phase covered reconnaissance, exploitation, and root access against a vulnerable target VM. Blue Team phase used Kibana to analyze attack logs, extract indicators of compromise, build visualizations, and produce hardening recommendations aligned with Security+ domains.
